summary: We noticed a common side effect in the astronauts' mental health during and after space missions. Soon, NASA is planning on sending crews on Mars and the Moon, so they are going to spend more time in space than ever. According to NASA's research - isolation, confinement and hostile closed environments are in the first five hazards of human spaceflight, so we decided to build a monitoring app that can be at the same time on the astronaut's Apple Watch, on the commander's console and even on the ground control screens. This app will use sensors on the watch to monitor the vital signs of the astronauts, such as Bpm, O2 levels and body temperature, but also, it is designed to measure stress levels, sleep length and it can track all astronauts moves and time spent in each room. All of the above will help design a behaviour profile for each astronaut in order to prevent depression and other mental anomalies. The way an astronaut thinks and acts should be monitored so we can prevent breakdowns and erratic behaviour.
details:
Our idea is to develop a platform for PCs that is in sync with astronauts' apple watches, in order to deal with mental health issues during missions, considering that they will become longer and more difficult. Our service will track medical vital signs, such as blood pressure, heart rate variability, body temperature, sleep and stress levels and more using smartwatches. But our idea does not stop here. We combine this information that we obtain automatically with information obtained from sensors and cameras inside the spaceship to track their daily behavior and mood and with information obtained directly from astronauts through questionnaires and online meetings with psychologists on earth. This allows Doctor Galactic to create a unique health profile tailored to every member of the crew. Because of the seamless integration with the apple watch, we can gather data such as vital medical signs during astronauts’ training effortlessly and faster than ever before. And our product can also help astronauts after they return to earth, because the majority of reported mental health problems appear after the flight, not in space.

The platform will be divided into 4 different types of menus, one for the commander, one for the astronauts, crew medical officer and one for mission control. When an anomaly regarding mental health is detected, Doctor Galactic will send an alert to the commander, informing him about the problem found and providing solutions on a first degree alert, the app will recommend physical exercise on a second degree alert, a calming and familiar environment using VR will be recommended to reduce stress levels. On third degree alert, an online meeting with a psychologist will be recommended, where further actions can be taken.

The technology is quite simple and it was already used by NASA in 2021 during an orbital space flight, it is affordable and intuitive, easy to use and it responds to a real concern that appeared the moment NASA planned longer spaceflights. Another benefit is that it offers permanent monitoring of the astronauts' health and also identify potential mental health issues and offer alternative solutions to medication.

We used the following tools : Claude code , Xcode , MacBooks , PowerPoint , Consensus.app , Gemini , Visual Studio Code, Chat Gpt.

We think our project is creative because it offers a solution that is easy to implement , using tools that are used by common people and the creation of a unique approach on identifying initial signs of mental health issues - creating a behavioural profile for every user by using a combination of data (number of hours of sleep, stress levels, tendency to isolate, loss of appetite, sadness, mood) that are likely to appear to people living for a long time in confined spaces, isolated from society. This way the behaviour that is out of the normal profile will be flagged and monitored, taking the necessary steps to deal with the problem, before it turns into something serious that can affect the crew's safety.

Our team considered the fact that long space flights are already planned for 2028 (Artemis IV with manned lunar crew) and a flight to Mars by 2030, and there is no data or research regarding the impact of long space flights on human mental health. Also, we considered using this app for other categories of people living for a long time in confined environments, like submarines or Antarctica (researchers who stay there for months to years).
